clue.text: Leisurely dial?

definitions.meaning: the straight sense: relaxed, unhurried, easy-going
the cryptic sense: the word dial is what you get when its mirror-image word is set back to front

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: the four-letter word meaning 'put down' written back to front spells dial, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid-back is the informal adjective for someone relaxed and unhurried in manner.

clue.text: One is treated after large wound

indicators.note: letters that are treated are processed or worked on, so the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is given medical treatment after suffering a large wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesion is a medical term for an injury or area of damaged tissue.

clue.text: Ramifications from Bill supporting naughty child

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath, so the bill goes below the child

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
a bill passed by parliament becomes an act

explanation.surface: The consequences of a piece of legislation propping up a badly behaved youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact means the effect or consequences something has, much as ramifications are its knock-on results.

clue.text: Be squeezing queen with fine bust

indicators.note: the outer word squeezes the others by holding them tightly between its letters

parts.note: taken as written
R for Regina, the Latin for queen
OK means all right, fine

explanation.surface: An instruction to clutch the queen with a splendid sculpted bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust is informal for having no money, which is exactly what broke means.

clue.text: Forms from Spain put in boxes

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the containers

parts.note: crates are wooden boxes for packing goods
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Paperwork from Spain being packed into containers.
explanation.definitionFit: To form something is to make or bring it into being, so forms is a synonym of creates.

clue.text: Get free top from emporium with small cloak

indicators.note: the top of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used
a cape is a sleeveless cloak

explanation.surface: A shopper grabs a top and a small cloak from a store without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to break loose or get away, a straightforward synonym for getting free.

clue.text: Remarkable bird concealing tail in nest

indicators.note: the bird hides the letter inside its own name

parts.note: the starling is a common speckled songbird

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

parts.note: only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A notable bird hiding its tail feathers in the nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling is surprising enough to be remarkable, an adjective of astonishment.

clue.text: Is a mean criminal caught? I forget

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for a person; this is what such a person might say

indicators.note: the letters behave criminally, being twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone accused of a mean crime pleads loss of memory when arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is something the answer would say, not a synonym for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesiac is a person suffering memory loss, who might well say 'I forget'.

clue.text: Prestigious European appeared — about time

indicators.note: the outer word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: seemed means appeared to be

explanation.surface: A distinguished European turned up after a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteemed means highly respected, which is what prestigious describes.

clue.text: So pup's barking, Edward presumed

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy

parts.note: taken as written
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward assumes the puppy is barking for some reason.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the dog's noise; it is also British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed and presumed both mean assumed to be true without proof.

clue.text: Minute silver hook — something attractive

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
to hook or net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: A tiny silver fishing hook that catches the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet attracts iron, and figuratively is anything that draws people in.

clue.text: Complain about a trip on a regular basis

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
taken as written

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

parts.note: only its second and fourth letters are used

explanation.surface: A grumble about a journey taken routinely.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault or grumble persistently, a synonym for complain.

clue.text: Arch Forest fans not following group of players

indicators.note: to fan something is to spread it out, scattering the letters
the abbreviation is left out of the words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Diehard supporters of Nottingham Forest who no longer follow the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Forest are Nottingham Forest, an English football club; 'fans' is a verb here, not supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is an ensemble of instrumental musicians, so a group of players.

clue.text: Liking Florida, perhaps moving south to the centre

indicators.note: the letter standing for south shifts from the front of the word into its middle

parts.note: Florida is one example of a US state

explanation.surface: Fondness for Florida, maybe relocating to the heart of the sunny south.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the opening S moves, landing in the middle of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste for something is a liking or preference for it.

clue.text: Unfortunately locked in mental asylum

indicators.note: the answer is shut up inside the words, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the answer sits across the join of these two words, its letters in order

explanation.surface: Sadly confined to a psychiatric institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection of regret, used to mean sadly or unfortunately.

clue.text: Places old cat gets surrounded by big ones

indicators.note: the old cat ends up inside the bigger animals' name

parts.note: following cat, the big ones are big cats such as lions
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly moggy is hemmed in by much larger felines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big ones' means big cats, borrowing 'cat' from earlier in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Locations and places are both nouns for particular positions or sites.

clue.text: Tommy's rabbit eating ivy mostly

definitions.note: read as Tommy is, i.e. a Tommy is one of these

indicators.note: the outer word swallows the shortened plant

parts.note: rabbit is British slang for chatter, as is prate

indicators.note: most of the word is used, the last letter dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tommy's pet rabbit is munching most of the ivy.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tommy is the old nickname for a British private soldier; rabbit and prate both mean talk idly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy Atkins was the traditional name for the ordinary British soldier of the lowest rank.

clue.text: Students might be seen in these university classes

definitions.text: Students might be seen in these
definitions.note: a plural noun phrase: things students wear

parts.note: uni is the informal short form
forms are school classes or year groups

explanation.surface: Undergraduates are seen in lectures at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen in' suggests attending; it means wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils at many schools wear standard outfits, so students may be seen dressed in them.

clue.text: Satire oddly put out someone we don't know

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, are kept

parts.note: only its odd letters are used
to put someone out is to annoy or anger them

explanation.surface: A satire strangely upset an unknown person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranger is a person unfamiliar to us, someone we have never met.

clue.text: Saw no sign of nerves with editor

parts.note: taken as written
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: An editor showed no trace of nervousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticed means observed or spotted, a past-tense synonym for saw.

clue.text: Rats scurry

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mild exclamation of annoyance
second meaning: to hurry or rush

explanation.walkthrough: Rats scurrying is the picture; rats here is an exclamation of irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash serves both as a mild oath of frustration and as a verb meaning rush off quickly.

clue.text: Talk about eastern maharishi?

definitions.note: a maharishi is one example, hence the question mark

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way

parts.note: gas is informal for idle chatter

explanation.surface: Discussing an Eastern spiritual guru.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharishi is a Hindu wise man or teacher, an example of a sage.

clue.text: Rambles stupidly, initially annoying people on the internet

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word goes first

parts.note: only its first letter is used
trolls post provocative messages online

explanation.surface: Someone babbles foolishly, irritating online trolls.
explanation.walkthrough: Rambles looks like rambling speech; it is gentle walks.
explanation.definitionFit: Strolls and rambles are both leisurely walks, used here as plural nouns or verbs.

clue.text: Distinguished Roman Emperor ignores us

indicators.note: the two letters are disregarded and left out

parts.note: Augustus was the first Roman emperor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A distinguished Roman emperor snubs the rest of us.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means venerable and respected, much like distinguished.

clue.text: Story that's unhistorical on purpose

parts.note: leg, or on, is the cricket term for the side of the field behind the batsman's legs
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: A tale that is deliberately inaccurate about history.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side of a cricket field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale popularly believed but not historically verified.

clue.text: Spread fear dropping last stone

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is let go

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for stone, an imperial weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: Fear of putting on weight, then losing the final stone, is spread about.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is informal for a lavish meal laid out, which is a feast.

clue.text: Ruth's cuter, weirdly, after husband's removed make-up

indicators.note: the remaining letters are arranged in a strange new order
the abbreviation is taken away from the words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
H for husband; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Ruth looks oddly prettier once her husband has wiped off her cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' looks like cosmetics; it means composition.
explanation.definitionFit: The make-up of something is its composition or the way it is put together.

clue.text: Stroke and lick someone's boots

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to grovel or behave obsequiously

explanation.walkthrough: Stroke suggests caressing a pet; it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Crawl names the freestyle swimming stroke and also means to fawn servilely on someone.

clue.text: River going west crossing over neighbourhood

indicators.note: the river runs across the letter, holding it inside
in an across answer going west means read right to left

parts.note: the Niger is a major river of West Africa
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A river flowing west across the district.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is an area or district, broadly a neighbourhood.

clue.text: Prayer guaranteed satisfaction

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request, as is a prayer
sure means certain, guaranteed

explanation.surface: An answered prayer brings certain contentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is the feeling of enjoyment or gratification, close to satisfaction.

clue.text: Parisian very stuck in ship creating tension

indicators.note: the French word is stuck inside the abbreviation

parts.note: SS is short for steamship
tres is French for very

explanation.surface: A Parisian stranded on a ship is causing friction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental or physical strain, so a synonym for tension.

clue.text: Remote island well ventilated? Not half!

parts.note: so, as in 'so, what now?', can stand for well

indicators.note: the first half of the word is left out

parts.note: only its second half is used

explanation.surface: A distant island that is breezy, very much so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so'; here it drops half a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated means far from other places or people, which is what remote describes.
